text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty ALERT fired: P0 - private-vpc controlplane heartbeats missing for customer BrightLeaf (prod). Trigger: controlplane-heartbeat-missing > 3m. PagerDuty incident: PD-88277

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-88277 created and sent to team: oncall

sara (oncall): acked via PagerDuty. I'm on it, logging in to the control plane and agent checks.

mike (oncall-2): noted. ping me if it looks like a network flapping issue - I'll stand by.

incident-bot: Current escalations: initial -> sara, 5m -> mike, 15m -> oncall-rotation.

sara (oncall): quick status: customer BrightLeaf has 12 private agents, 6 reporting heartbeats, 6 missing since ~02:05 UTC. Running quick health check on control-plane API.

sara (oncall): runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/private-vpc/heartbeat-missing. Following the 'agent-stalls' section.

juan (netops): @sara can you paste the agent side logs (last 2 minutes) from one of the affected hosts? I'll check peering and firewall counters.

sara (oncall): grabbing logs from brightleaf-agent-07 (one of the missing) - here's tail: 

```
Mar 03 02:04:55 redwood-agent[3124]: heartbeat sent to controlplane.x.y.z:443 status=timeout
Mar 03 02:05:01 redwood-agent[3124]: reconnecting... attempt=1
Mar 03 02:05:05 redwood-agent[3124]: failed to establish TLS: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
Mar 03 02:05:10 redwood-agent[3124]: backoff 5s
```

sara (oncall): hmm TLS errors, might be cert rotation related. But control-plane logs show sporadic accept from those hosts.

mike (oncall-2): @juan could be an MTU / middlebox rewriting TLS? But cert errors usually point to trust chain.

juan (netops): I'm running quick connectivity tests from the peering router into BrightLeaf VPC. ping mostly fine, no packet loss. Running `tcpdump` on the peering interface for TLS handshake failures.

zoe (support): I've opened a customer-facing note: "We are investigating intermittent control plane connectivity for some agents. No API requests are impacted for other customers." Will update once we have root cause.

sara (oncall): trying to restart the agent service on brightleaf-agent-07 to re-establish TLS handshakes. Running: `sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent`

sara (oncall): service status after restart: 

```
● redwood-agent.service - Redwood private agent
   Loaded: loaded (/etc/systemd/system/redwood-agent.service; enabled; vendor preset: enabled)
   Active: active (running) since Tue 2026-03-03 02:08:12 UTC; 12s ago
   Main PID: 4128 (redwood-agent)
   Logs: 
     Mar 03 02:08:13 redwood-agent[4128]: TLS handshake completed, certs validated, agent registered id=bf-07
     Mar 03 02:08:13 redwood-agent[4128]: heartbeat interval=30s
```

sara (oncall): brightleaf-agent-07 reconnected and heartbeating. Good sign. I'm rolling restarts on two other missing hosts (05,09) one at a time.

mike (oncall-2): good. If restarts fix >80% we probably have stale cert cache or ephemeral port exhaustion during rotation. Keep notes.

juan (netops): tcpdump shows a burst of RSTs to controlplane from those agent IPs around 02:04-02:06. Could be transient firewall rule enforcement or path MTU causing handshake truncation. I'll check firewall logs for policy re-evals.

sara (oncall): restarted 05 -> reconnected. restarted 09 -> reconnected. Currently 9/12 agents healthy, 3 still missing (02,11,12).

incident-bot: PagerDuty escalation in 5 minutes if not acknowledged by secondary.

sara (oncall): trying a different approach for the remaining three: collect `openssl s_client` output against controlplane from one host to see certificate chain and SNI.

sara (oncall): output snippet from brightleaf-agent-02: 

```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Redwood, CN = Redwood Root CA
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
SSL handshake has read 1387 bytes and written 460 bytes
```

sara (oncall): verify error indicates the host doesn't have the root CA in its trust store. But we've not rolled out any CA changes for BrightLeaf. Need to check recent config pushes.

mike (oncall-2): @sara any recent config pushes to BrightLeaf's agent config? Could be an automated cert bundle update that missed some hosts.

sara (oncall): checking config-service logs... There was a config push at 01:58 UTC to brightleaf namespace tied to a routine cert metadata refresh. Most hosts applied OK; a small subset failed due to transient apt lock (weird). Filing a follow-up.

zoe (support): I'm drafting a short customer update: "We're continuing an investigation; some agents experienced failed TLS handshakes after a routine configuration refresh. We're restarting affected agents and monitoring. Will follow up with a root cause in our incident report." Happy to send once engineering confirms.

juan (netops): firewall logs show a transient policy re-eval at 02:05 that coincided with config push. Looks like the policy engine temporarily dropped established connections during enforcement refresh. That could explain the RSTs. We're correlating with config-service events.

sara (oncall): tl;dr: two factors: config push attempted at 01:58, some hosts failed to fetch CA bundle; network policy re-eval at 02:05 caused RSTs while agents retried -> left some agents with incomplete trust chain. Mitigation: restart agents that failed to apply config, and re-run config apply (forced) for the brightleaf namespace.

mike (oncall-2): recommend we also temporarily disable the policy re-eval auto-apply for that peering for next 1hr while we stabilize. @juan can you hold off further re-applies?

juan (netops): I can hold scheduled enforcement refreshes for this peering for 30 minutes. Paused at 02:20 UTC.

sara (oncall): I've forced config apply for the three remaining hosts and restarted their agents. Monitoring heartbeat counts...

sara (oncall): all three reconnected. 12/12 agents healthy as of 02:24 UTC. Heartbeat latency normalized.

pagerduty-bot: PD-88277 acknowledged and resolved by sara (oncall) at 02:25 UTC.

sara (oncall): marking incident as mitigated. Creating bug and postmortem ticket: INC-49321, linking logs, runbook gaps. Action items: 1) add retry logic for config-service when hosts report apt lock; 2) make enforcement refresh non-disruptive for peering interfaces; 3) improve agent telemetry to flag missing trust chain preemptively.

zoe (support): sending customer update now: "Issue mitigated; all agents reconnected. We will follow up with RCA and timeline"

mike (oncall-2): nice work. I'm going to grab the handoff notes and pick this up for the postmortem later (esp. the config-service failure mode).

sara (oncall): handing off to mike for postmortem write-up. I'm going to sign off for a quick break but will check back in an hour.

mike (oncall-2): taking ownership for the RCA write-up. Will ping if we need further logs.

incident-bot: Incident PD-88277 closed. :white_check_mark:

sara (oncall): closing thread. Thanks everyone.
